item.title: Fernandes And Cunha Get 8 | Manchester United Players Rated In Hard-Fought Draw Vs Aston Villa

Nicolas Jackson doubled his side’s lead in the fourth minute, but Bruno Fernandes got a goal back for Man United from the penalty spot in the 16th minute. Youri Tielemans scored the all-important equaliser for Man United in the 44th minute as both sides went into the half-time break with a 2-2 scoreline. John McGinn scored from the penalty spot in the 48th minute before Leon Goretzka got his name on the scoresheet as well just five minutes later. Joshua Zirkzee got a goal back for the Mancunian giants in injury time before Patrick Dorgu rescued a point for Man United in the dying embers of the contest. The match finished with Man United securing a hard-fought 4-4 draw at the Theatre of Dreams. Let’s take a look at how each Manchester United player fared during the clash against the Villans. He made a couple of solid saves at the back and conceded four goals this evening. RB: Noussair Mazraoui – 7/10 Mazraoui did his fair share of defending and made two key chances going forward. He has an assist to his name. CB: Leny Yoro – 5.5/10 He was far from convincing on the defensive end of the field and made a costly error at the back. CB: Harry Maguire – 6/10 Maguire failed to impress in the first half and was substituted at half-time. item.title: Mercedes crowned 2026 F1 constructors' champion at Brazilian GP
item.description: Motorsport photo Mercedes has won the 2026 Formula 1 constructors' championship, sealing the title at the Brazilian Grand Prix at Interlagos. Antonelli and Russell started second and seventh on the grid, after the Briton took a five-place grid penalty. While Antonelli took the lead from polesitter Lando Norris at the start of the race and extended his lead to five seconds over the first seven laps, he later spun into Turn 1, giving Norris the opportunity to retake the position. Antonelli started to drop down the order as he complained that "the car is pulling on one side when accelerating." After heavy rainfall in the closing laps of the race, Kimi Antonelli and George Russell finished fourth and fifth, which was enough to put the team out of reach of Ferrari, whose drivers Charles Leclerc and Lewis Hamilton finished seventh and ninth, respectively. Lando Norris won the Brazilian Grand Prix and the McLaren driver was joined on the podium by Red Bull's Max Verstappen and Isack Hadjar. Mercedes arrived in Sao Paulo 126 points clear of Ferrari and needed to leave with a lead of 129 points. The title completes a championship double for the team, one week after Antonelli clinched the drivers' crown at the Mexican Grand Prix to become the youngest world champion in the history of F1. The 2026 title is the Brackley outfit's ninth constructors' championship, after already winning in 2014, 2015, 2016, 2017, 2018, 2019, 2020 and 2021. item.title: Man Utd rescue Villa draw with incredible fightback, Chelsea stunned
item.description: Manchester United defender Patrick Dorgu (2nd R) celebrates after scoring against Aston Villa (Darren Staples) Manchester United rescued an incredible 4-4 draw against Aston Villa as two stoppage-time goals gave Michael Carrick renewed hope of avoiding the sack, while Chelsea suffered a shock 1-0 loss at Sunderland on Sunday. United boss Carrick was seconds away from heading into the international break on the back of another devastating defeat that would surely have led to his dismissal. But Carrick's side struck twice in the six minutes of additional time through Joshua Zirkzee and Patrick Dorgu to leave their manager's future still uncertain. United are in the relegation zone and have not won in their last eight Premier League matches, so it is far from sure that Carrick will survive the axe. He had earned a stay of execution when United's hierarchy allowed him to remain in charge despite last weekend's loss at Chelsea. United responded by ending a nine-match winless run in all competitions as they came from two goals down to beat Roma 3-2 in the Champions League on Tuesday. But United, who have only three wins in 15 games this season, were back in turmoil when they fell 2-0 down against Villa in the first four minutes at Old Trafford. Alysson struck in the first minute with a shot that squirmed under United keeper Senne Lammens. Nicolas Jackson slotted in the second three minutes later after a weak save from Lammens pushed the ball into his path. Bruno Fernandes got one back with a 16th-minute penalty after Boubacar Kamara fouled Matheus Cunha before former Villa midfielder Youri Tielemans slammed in United's 44th-minute equaliser. Villa's John McGinn converted a 48th-minute penalty following Diogo Dalot's clumsy challenge on Alysson. Leon Goretzka poked in Villa's fourth from close-range after United's Leny Yoro headed against his own crossbar in the 53rd minute. Yet Zirkzee's stoppage-time finish gave United hope and Dorgu headed their dramatic equaliser in the final seconds after a weak punch from Villa keeper Zion Suzuki. Carrick wore a bewildered look on his face as he walked down the tunnel towards an uncertain future, with United next in action at Liverpool on November 22. Chelsea arrived at the Stadium of Light hoping to bolster their bid to qualify for the Champions League via a top-four finish. Instead, they departed red-faced after an embarrassing loss to third-bottom Sunderland, who celebrated a league victory for only the second time this season. Fifth-placed Chelsea have already been beaten four times in 10 league matches under former Real Madrid boss Xabi Alonso. - Liverpool back on track - Chelsea were rocked in the 36th minute when Enzo Le Fee converted a penalty after Brian Brobbey was up-ended by Levi Colwill. "We were not creating enough chances in the final third against the low block. We were not controlling and sustaining the attack there," Alonso said. Liverpool got back on track with a 3-1 win at lowly Crystal Palace.

Brighton extended their superb start to the season, climbing to second place with a 2-0 win against Brentford at the Amex Stadium. Diego Gomez put Brighton ahead early on before Brentford striker Igor Thiago was sent off. Pascal Gross doubled Brighton's advantage with a 42nd minute penalty. item.description: By Duncan Bech England delivered the backlash promised in support of their under-fire head coach Steve Borthwick as Henry Pollock starred in a record 45-22 rout of Australia at Twickenham . Reeling from a report published on Thursday claiming that Borthwick presided over a toxic environment during the July tour, seven tries were engineered in a show of unity from his players. One of the best attacking displays of the Borthwick era was lit up by electric performances from Pollock and Immanuel Feyi-Waboso, who crossed three times between them. The blow of seeing the explosive Feyi-Waboso limp off with a leg injury at half-time having repeatedly punched holes in Australia’s defence was softened by his replacement Pollock shining on his debut on the wing. item.title: Hamza Zahoor's century overshadows Arjun Rajput's 107 as Pakistan U19 pull off thrilling three-wicket win over India
item.description: Pakistan Under-19 pulled off a memorable three-wicket victory over arch-rivals India in the ACC Men's U19 Asia Cup 2026, with captain Hamza Zahoor producing a composed century to guide his side home in a tense chase at Al Amerat, Oman, on Sunday. Chasing 209, Pakistan found themselves in deep trouble at 63/5, with India's bowlers threatening to take the game away. However, Zahoor held his nerve and led a remarkable recovery, stitching together a crucial 107-run partnership with Hasnain Abbas Dar to turn the contest around. Dar contributed 38 off 67 balls before departing at 168/6, giving India another opening. But Zahoor continued to anchor the chase, eventually taking Pakistan across the finish line with three wickets to spare. The result handed Pakistan an important Group A victory over their traditional rivals and strengthened their position in the race for a place in the semi-finals. Arjun Rajput's fighting century rescues India Earlier, India endured a disastrous start after captain Lakshya Raichandani was dismissed for a duck in the first over. Pakistan's pace attack kept the pressure on, reducing India to 42/4 and then 86/5. With the top order back in the pavilion, Arjun Rajput took responsibility and launched a counter-attack. The left-hander smashed 107 off 85 deliveries, striking 11 fours and five sixes, to give India a fighting total. Rajput found useful support from Anvay Dravid (10) and Manal Chauhan (11), but his dismissal at 170/7 in the 36th over triggered another collapse. India lost their remaining wickets for 38 runs and were bowled out for 208 in 46.3 overs. Kavya Patel's 23 provided a late contribution, helping India cross the 200-run mark. Pakistan bowlers keep India under control Pakistan's bowling unit played a major role in restricting India to 208. Ali Raza led the attack with three wickets, while Rizwanullah and Niqab Shafiq also claimed three wickets apiece. The early strikes from Raza and the pressure maintained by Mohammad Sayyam put India on the back foot, before the spinners tightened their grip in the middle overs. India fight back but Zahoor stands firm India did not make Pakistan's chase easy. Manal Chauhan picked up two wickets, while Kavya Patel and Mohit Ulva also struck as Pakistan slipped to 61/5. But Zahoor's partnership with Dar changed the course of the match. Even after Dar's dismissal, the Pakistan captain remained in control and completed the job, sealing a three-wicket win for his side.

item.title: Aggies Underdogs At Home Against Tennessee
item.description: Texas A&M was competitive against South Carolina, but the Aggies ultimately were unable to find victory as they fell to the Gamecocks 17-9. Now Texas A&M will return to Kyle Field to face the Tennessee Volunteers. Per FanDuel , the Aggies are 2.5-point underdogs when Tennessee comes to town. The over / under is set at 42.5 points. Tennessee was dominant last time out as the Volunteers thrashed Kentucky 34-6. UT is 7-2 on the season, with the losses coming at home against Texas and on the road against South Carolina. The Volunteers lead the all-time series against the Aggies 3-2. The last time Tennessee came to College Station was in 2016, when the Aggies won a thriller over the Vols 45-38. That contest was also the first trip Tennessee ever made to Kyle Field. Texas A&M only being a 2.5-point underdog against Tennessee this week comes as a bit of a surprise to me, given the recent performances turned in by both teams, but maybe Vegas knows something we don’t. If Mike Elko and the Aggies are going to go bowling this year, they will need to find a way to win two of the next three contests. We’ll see if Texas A&M can pull off a shocker at Kyle Field.

item.title: Serie A line-ups: Fiorentina vs. Juventus
item.description: Serie A line-ups: Fiorentina vs. Juventus Nick Woltemade is declared fit to start in attack for Juventus against Fiorentina in Serie A on Sunday evening, as Paolo Vanoli makes just one alteration to his winning side. It kicks off at 19.45 GMT (20.45 CET). You can follow the action as it unfolds on the Football Italia Liveblog. REGGIO NELL’EMILIA, ITALY – NOVEMBER 02: Franco Mastantuono of ACF Fiorentina celebrates scoring his team’s third goal during the Serie A match between US Sassuolo and ACF Fiorentina at Mapei Stadium – Citta’ del Tricolore on November 02, 2026 in Reggio nell’Emilia, Italy. (Photo by Emmanuele Ciancaglini/Getty Images) Hosts Fiorentina find themselves in 15th place in the Serie A standings ahead of kick-off. They have won two, drawn two and lost six of their opening 10 league games this season, but are unbeaten across their last two, claiming a 4-2 victory over Sassuolo last weekend. Juventus are in seventh place after the first 10 league games of the season after five wins, two draws and three defeats at the start of the Serie A season. They picked up a much-needed 2-0 victory over Napoli last time out in the league and have since beaten AZ Alkmaar 2-1 away from home in the Europa League. ALKMAAR, NETHERLANDS – NOVEMBER 05: Teun Koopmeiners of Juventus celebrates with teammates after scoring his team’s first goal during the UEFA Europa League 2026/27 League Phase MD4 match between AZ Alkmaar and Juventus at AZ Stadion on November 05, 2026 in Alkmaar, Netherlands. (Photo by Lars Baron/Getty Images) The Bianconeri still have a hefty injury list that includes Kenan Yildiz, Khephren Thuram, Manuel Locatelli, Nico Gonzalez and Francisco Conceicao. Nick Woltemade is declared fit despite struggling with a bout of flu , and is included in Sunday’s starting line-up alongside Randal Kolo Muani in attack. Jeremie Boga completes the attacking trident. TURIN, ITALY – NOVEMBER 01: Jeremie Boga of Juventus celebrates scoring his team’s second goal during the Serie A match between Juventus and SSC Napoli at Allianz Stadium on November 01, 2026 in Turin, Italy. (Photo by Valerio Pennicino/Getty Images) Paolo Vanoli has made just one change to his side that defeated Sassuolo last weekend: Pedro Goncalves is introduced in midfield in place of Marco Brescianini. Kick-off is due at 19.45 GMT (20.45 CET). Fiorentina (4-2-3-1) : De Gea; Jiménez, Dragusin, Viery, Joao Mario; Ndour, Oulai; Mastantuono, Gonçalves, Njie; Pellegrino. Juventus (4-3-3) : Vicario; Kalulu, Bremer, Lucumí, Cabal; McKennie, Douglas Luiz, Koopmeiners; Kolo Muani, Woltemade, Boga.

Magic Johnson is celebrating a major milestone with his HIV diagnosis over 30 years ago. The retired NBA legend held a press conference in 1991 when he announced that he had been diagnosed with HIV. On Saturday, Nov. 7, Johnson shared that he is thankful for how far he’s come since his original announcement. “Look at how far God has brought me since my HIV announcement 35 years ago! It is truly because of His grace and mercy that I am still here and thriving,” Johnson wrote on X. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) “God never gave up on me, and I kept the faith,” he continued. “I am thankful for all of the prayers from my family, friends, and fans throughout the years, and I am a living witness that there’s nothing too hard for God.” Johnson learned of his diagnosis when he went to get a physical ahead of the 1991-92 NBA season. When he heard of the diagnosis for the first time, he told CBS Mornings in 2024 that he was “devastated.” His wife, Earletha “Cookie” Johnson,” was pregnant at the time and while their son, Earvin “EJ” Johnson III was found HIV-negative, he shared that telling her the news was difficult. “It was hard because I loved her so much and I hated to hurt her,” he said. He didn’t play a regular-season game that year but he did perform in the NBA All-Star team in 1992 when fans voted him in for a spot on the roster. “It proved to be the right decision,” he said. “It helped people who were living with not just HIV and AIDS, but with any disease, that you can live on, you can be — live a productive life.” Since he learned of his own diagnosis, he has had made a huge difference in supporting those who have been diagnosed with HIV/AIDS. He started the Magic Johnson Foundation to help others with their fight against the virus. The foundation has provided more than 40,000 free HIV screenings nationwide. It also partnered with the AIDS Healthcare Foundation to create HIV/AIDS clinics in California and Florida. The foundation also has created the Earvin Johnson Sr. scholarship program to aid students at Michigan State University. item.description: Manager delighted to get important win over Kilmarnock Celtic took all three points with a hard-fought 1-0 home win over Kilmarnock this afternoon. Liam Scales scored the all-important goal, steering home a Camilo Duran cross in the 25th minute, and despite missing a second-half penalty, Martin O’Neill’s side maintained their clean sheet to get the win and restore their four-point lead going into the international break. Speaking to CelticPlayer after the game, the Celtic manager said: “I’m delighted to have won the game after Thursday night's exertions. “I thought that we were not at our very, very best today although, actually having said that, we created a number of good chances in the game and Sam Johnstone made a double save for us in the first 90 seconds of the game.” And the manager praised the match-winner for his goal and overall performance throughout the 90 minutes. “Scales has been absolutely wonderful,” the manager said. “I don't know what he's been like at the club before that – I'm sure he's a really fine player – but in my year in the game he’s been sensational for us. “He's a centre-half, but sometimes I'm expecting him to play the ball like an inside forward or something like that, but overall he's been really terrific. “He's come up with some big, big goals, but he's also come up with big, big moments defensively for us during my time.” Fixtures Celtic Vs. Kilmarnock - Sun, Nov 8th 2026, 16:00 Final score: 1 - 0

item.title: Heat's Erik Spoelstra takes massive shot at Doc Rivers for Giannis Antetokounmpo comments
item.description: Heat's Erik Spoelstra takes massive shot at Doc Rivers for Giannis Antetokounmpo comments originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Miami Heat entered the offseason with a mission to acquire some big names who could help position the organization for success this season and potentially beyond. Miami made several significant moves that had fans excited about what the team could accomplish. The biggest move of them all was acquiring an NBA champion. The Heat pulled off a blockbuster trade for Giannis Antetokounmpo. “The Milwaukee Bucks are trading franchise icon Giannis Antetokounmpo and Bobby Portis to the Miami Heat for Tyler Herro, Kel'el Ware, Jaime Jaquez Jr., Kasparas Jakucionis, three first-round picks (including No. 13 in Tuesday's NBA draft), one pick swap and one second-round pick, sources told ESPN. The Heat are sending to Milwaukee unprotected first-rounders in 2031 and 2033 along with No. 13, a pick swap in 2030 and a 2033 second-rounder, according to sources," ESPN's Shams Charania wrote. The start of the season has brought some challenges for Antetokounmpo, particularly after his former head coach, Doc Rivers, recently made some critical comments about what it was like coaching him. Rivers described the two-time MVP as a difficult player to coach. “He's interesting. He's not easy. He's not easy because he plays at this crazy downhill pace. He's really a difficult guy. ... He has this great passing ability, but he doesn't necessarily have this super IQ at the same time. It's really a strange thing, and he really has one way: downhill, force, force. Every play, he wants to force it,” Rivers said. Heat head coach Erik Spoelstra wasn't going to let those comments go unanswered. He responded to Rivers, making it clear that Antetokounmpo's development is now Miami's responsibility. “Look, I like Doc, and I respect him, this is our business now. We went into the season thinking that that would be a process, playing with somebody (Giannis) that commands so much attention. That’s a different style than some of the guys that have come here, that have played before,” Spoelstra said. There is no doubt that Miami is going to stand behind its major offseason addition, but it is rare to see Spoelstra publicly respond to another coach in this manner. The Heat view Antetokounmpo as a cornerstone of the organization, and Spoelstra is making it clear that the team is committed to helping him succeed. Spoelstra understands that the season is far from over and isn't going to let outside criticism become a distraction for his team. A head coach is naturally going to stand behind his players, and Spoelstra has made it clear that Antetokounmpo has his full support. item.title: Marc Marquez unveils simple plan as he closes in on MotoGP title: "Train, eat, sleep, repeat"
item.description: Motorsport photo Marc Marquez has revealed a change in approach as he looks to seal the MotoGP world championship when the series returns to Europe in two weeks. After securing 32 of a possible 37 points over the Qatar Grand Prix weekend, Marquez is poised to wrap up the championship at the Portuguese Grand Prix in two weeks. Read Also: MotoGP Qatar GP: Marco Bezzecchi wins as Marc Marquez has title triumph delayed The factory Ducati rider travels to the penultimate round of the series with a lead of 60 points over Aprilia's Jorge Martin , who is in turn 14 points clear of team-mate Marco Bezzecchi . While both Aprilias are still in mathematical contention, Martin remains a long shot, while Bezzecchi, in his own words, "needs a miracle". But the job is not officially done for Marquez. A win in the sprint at Portimao will certainly be enough for Marquez to wrap up the title. But Marc might be able secure the crown with only a middling result in the sprint - depending on what his opponents do. And if he can't get the job done on the Saturday in Portugal, it's likely that he won't need to deliver much on the Sunday to put the seal on the championship. Enea Bastianini, Red Bull KTM Tech 3, Pedro Acosta, Red Bull KTM Factory Racing, Marc Marquez, Ducati Team Enea Bastianini, Red Bull KTM Tech 3, Pedro Acosta, Red Bull KTM Factory Racing, Marc Marquez, Ducati Team With these relatively simple requirements in mind, Marquez says it's time to switch off the 'attack' mentality he has adopted and focus on getting the points he needs. item.description: Denny Medley-Imagn Images Missouri football’s Eli Drinkwitz really wanted to rip refs after Texas game, but he didn’t appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Missouri football team suffered a tough defeat on Saturday to Texas. Missouri was defeated, 34-20. Tigers head coach Eli Drinkwitz wasn’t happy after the game. “If I say what I want to say, I’m going to get fined until I don’t have any retirement, and I’m not going to do that. I’m not going to blame the officials. That would be disrespectful to Coach Sarkisian and his team,” Drinkwitz said, per On3. Missouri dropped to 6-3 on the season. The Tigers finished the game allowing 401 total yards of offense to the Longhorns. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) The Tigers struggled to move the chains. Missouri finished the game going just 3-for-16 on third-down conversions. The team also couldn’t take advantage when Texas made mistakes. “I could hear the talk getting on the plane yesterday. I could hear the talk when we got here. Nobody believed we’d win the game,” Texas head coach Steve Sarkisian said, per ESPN. “Nobody thought we were going to come here and win the game. Nobody thought we were tough enough at the line of scrimmage.” Texas improved to 7-2 on the year. There were some questionable calls during Missouri-Texas game At least one college football analyst feels Drinkwitz’s pain. That is Jesse Palmer from ESPN. Palmer felt that a play that was called a fumble on Texas should have instead been ruled an incomplete pass. Because the play was ruled a fumble, Texas was actually able to gain yards on the play. The ball moved downfield . “If you’re a Missouri fan, if you’re Eli Drinkwitz, you are livid because it does feel like a lot of these calls are going against Missouri today,” Palmer said, per Awful Announcing, regarding the officiating in the game. Missouri’s loss effectively ends their chances at making the College Football Playoff this season. The Tigers are now 3-3 in SEC play. The team’s losses this season are to Texas, Ole Miss and Mississippi State. Missouri next plays Georgia on Saturday. item.title: Wagner encouraged by Köln’s attacking display despite Leverkusen defeat
item.description: Wagner encouraged by Köln’s attacking display despite Leverkusen defeat The Billy Goats were unable to come away with a positive result, but Wagner was encouraged by the chances his side created against a strong Leverkusen outfit, while admitting they lacked the necessary quality in the final third at times. “Both teams played with a lot of passion. We had chances in the opening minutes to score a goal ourselves. Sometimes today we lacked that final touch, that final pass,” Wagner explained after the game. Despite the disappointment of defeat, the Köln coach was keen to emphasise the positives, insisting his players should take confidence from their ability to repeatedly threaten a very good opposition. “We have to keep attacking with real passion. We saw that a lot today. Today we managed to create chances against a very good team time and again. That should give us confidence,” he added. Wagner also highlighted the potential for further improvement in the attacking department, with the expected return of Ragnar Ache following the international break providing another boost to Köln’s options in the final third. “We’re looking forward to Ragy returning after the international break so we can become even more dangerous in the opposition’s box,” he said. “We can still create even more dangerous chances. We know that, and we’re continuing to work on it. But I think everyone in the stadium felt today that the boys keep trying and give it their all.” There was also praise for Malek El Mala, who continued his promising run of form with another goal contribution. Wagner was particularly pleased with the youngster’s progress and the opportunity to see him sharing the pitch with his brother. “I’m happy for Malek - two games, two goal contributions. That shows you can earn playing time through hard work. I’m happy for the two brothers, who are out on the pitch together and giving it their all,” Wagner remarked. The Köln coach also reserved some encouraging words for Mikey Moore, praising the Tottenham loanee’s commitment and willingness to get stuck into the contest against Leverkusen. “You could tell he threw himself into the challenges. He knew that would be important today. I’m sure he’ll get more opportunities to reward himself with points for scoring,” Wagner concluded.

item.title: Leverkusen win derby 2-1 at Cologne as Freiburg go third
item.description: Bayer Leverkusen's Aleix Garcia scoring his side's first goal during the German Bundesliga soccer match between 1. FC Cologne and Bayer Leverkusen at the RheinEnergieStadion. (is associated with: «Leverkusen win derby 2-1 at Cologne as Freiburg go third») Rolf Vennenbernd/dpa An early goal from Aleix García and a late strike from Patrik Schick gave Bayer Leverkusen the bragging rights after a 2-1 derby win at neighbours Cologne on Sunday. The Werkself moved up to fifth in the Bundesliga table ahead of the international break while Cologne are 15th, just above the relegation places. Freiburg reclaimed third spot after Rani Khedira's own goal and Yuito Suzuki's fifth of the league season set up a 2-0 home victory over third-bottom Union Berlin. Vincenzo Grifo even had the luxury of missing a penalty. The Black Forest side, who went back above RB Leipzig, have never qualified for the Champions League but are well-placed after nine of 34 games. In Cologne, Leverkusen bounced back from losing 1-0 at home to Marseille in the Europa League on Thursday and two straight Bundesliga defeats. Garcia netted with a sumptuous free-kick on 7 minutes and Schick used his power to score on 85 having previously had a goal ruled out for a handball. "It was a great shot," García told streaming platform DAZN. "We practise in training when we can. This is something that I did all my career. Happy to score my first goal in the Bundesliga (this season)." Germany winger Saïd El Mala pulled one back in stoppage time, but it came too late for the hosts. It could get worse for Cologne if second-bottom Schalke prevail at Hoffenheim in the late game and overhaul the Billygoats. In Saturday's main programme of matches, leaders Bayern Munich and Borussia Dortmund beat Mainz and Elversberg 2-1 respectively to remain undefeated.

item.description: Ken Blaze-Imagn Images The trade of Jaylen Brown from the Boston Celtics to the Philadelphia 76ers created a mix of shock and intense debate across the NBA. Fans felt outraged, but front offices focused on a heated debate over Brown’s true value on the court. This debate centered on how modern data analysis of players in a league flooded with information works. Brown is a five-time All-Star and a former Finals MVP who finished sixth in regular-season MVP voting in 2026 after averaging a career-best 28.7 points per game, according to ESPN . Despite these impressive traditional numbers, advanced statistics were more skeptical of his stardom. In seven of Brown’s 10 Boston seasons, the Celtics achieved a superior net rating when he sat rather than played, covering each of the final four. Cleaning the Glass, which removes garbage time, is the source for all on/off figures in this article. With Brown set to face his former team for the first time Tuesday at 8 p.m. ET on NBC/Peacock, it’s the right time to examine the divide between his reputation and the data. The Basics of On and Off Data A modern NBA front office uses vast amounts of data to evaluate every player in the league. Teams track points, rebounds, assists, shot quality, pick-and-roll frequency, and isolation efficiency. While individual data points are nearly endless, the objective remains the same. A front office should identify players who help the team outscore opponents rather than players who just collect strong statistics in a vacuum. Players boasting top individual stats frequently deliver the greatest winning impact, though this is not always the case. These mismatches can lead to different, sometimes counterintuitive, evaluations of players. Exemplary on/off numbers throughout their careers were no surprise to those role players. Public perception of a defensive impact reputation often requires a very long time to stabilize. An Eastern Conference team analyst stated that 10,000 possessions, roughly two seasons of starter data, represent the minimum sample size before on/off data becomes useful. This caution runs counter to the modern media cycle’s incessant demand for information and immediate answers. The public often wants to see results right away without waiting for a large sample to form. The Problem with Small Samples Because of the pressure to find answers quickly, many people jump to conclusions based on limited data. According to the East analyst, the public should not access on/off data this early in the season. It should be banned. I think it’s a disservice to the discourse. This statement highlights the frustration many feel when raw numbers are used to judge players too soon. IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Transforming on/off data from a raw metric into a useful tool requires patience and context. A Western Conference team executive observed that the issue involves inherent biases of all sorts, including the sample size problem. Whatever narrative you wish to construct, you can find confirmation, which is why an executive for a Western Conference team called it astrology for NBA professionals. This bias allows people to pick the data that supports their pre-existing opinion about a player. For this reason, professionals often look for more sophisticated methods that adjust for these variables. The goal is to isolate the player’s actual impact from the noise of small sample sizes and team context. This describes stats like RAPM, which incorporate various adjustments to refine raw data. This process helps teams make better decisions by looking deeper than simple on/off splits. Two years ago, Snarr noted that the key factor is how frequently and consistently players play together. This consistency makes the data more reliable and accurate over time. Kostya Medvedovsky, a model builder, stated that RAPM could reduce the convincing timeline for on/off from 10 years to maybe two years. By isolating impact, these adjusted metrics enable much quicker, more accurate player analysis. This shift in methodology has changed how teams evaluate talent and build their rosters. The ability to get a clearer picture faster helps front offices make trades and sign players with more confidence. However, the process can lean more toward art than science, making the trickier question how to weigh these different types of information. The Western executive remarked that legitimate debate and variance amongst the nerds emerge there, in his view. For a player like Jaylen Brown, this variance in interpretation played a major role in his departure from Boston. The Celtics’ internal view of his value likely differed from the public perception of his stardom. Medvedovsky said the Jaylen Brown case is, in some ways, the purest proof of this. Lessons from the adjusted on/off metrics appear to have permeated most front-office thinking. The trade was not just about scoring numbers but about how the team performed with him on the floor. The data suggested that the Celtics could be more effective with different lineup combinations. This analytical approach led to a blockbuster move that surprised many fans but made sense to those who trusted the adjusted stats. item.title: Julián Alvarez’s Atlético redemption arc in full focus for visit of Barcelona
item.description: Top spot is up for grabs in Sunday’s heavyweight clash as the Spider faces the team that tried to trap him last summer Julián Alvarez said sorry but forgiveness must be earned on the field and Sunday would be the perfect place. At 9pm at the Metropolitano, Atlético Madrid play Barcelona. It is the biggest match in Spain right now, a place at the top of the table awaiting the winner; it is also the game the striker they call the Spider planned to play on the other side. That, Alvarez said in Dallas, was his “dream”. Denied that, he must defeat the men he wanted to join to win back the supporters he wanted to walk out on, no better opportunity than now. He has beaten them before. Last season, Atlético knocked Barcelona out of the Copa del Rey and Champions League . Alvarez scored both times but beneath the surface something had shifted in him and by the time the World Cup came round he admitted his desire to leave for Catalonia. That day, after Argentina beat Algeria, he didn’t name Barcelona and he didn’t need to; everyone knew. “It’s not the time to talk about this but nor can I hide,” he said. “I spoke with the people I needed to and the best thing for everyone is a transfer.” Continue reading...

item.title: Rise of the ‘schooligans’: how a wave of antisocial behaviour threatens non-league football
item.description: Teenage ultras are increasingly causing disorder and communities fear it will not be long before it becomes something more dangerous It is five past three on Saturday afternoon and the teenage ultras of Hednesford Town are running late. They have arrived in Chester for their team’s National League North fixture and have hailed taxis, determined to make their presence felt at the ground. But word appears to have got out about their arrival. As one car turns away from the city’s charming half-timbered houses and into narrow residential streets, half a dozen local youths appear, haring round the corner in balaclavas. They try to attack the cab and chase after it as it pulls away. The smell of pyro is everywhere. As the taxi finally gets clear, the Chester gang stops in the middle of the road, shouting and gesticulating. One lad, no older than 16, pulls a long blade from inside his trousers and brandishes it. The incident ended there and no one was hurt, though a police investigation has been launched. The match went off without trouble too and the Hednesford gang – known at home as the “schooligans” – were escorted safely back to the station by Cheshire police. It was just another weekend in English non-league football, where a wave of antisocial behaviour is causing concern and leading the UK Football Policing Unit (UKFPU) to declare it its “most important” priority. As the disorder continues, a question remains: how long will it be before teenage trouble-making becomes something more dangerous? Continue reading...

item.title: Football Daily | You want proper football? Here are the FA Cup first-round ties to look out for
item.description: Sign up now! Sign up now! Sign up now? Sign up now! For the FA Cup, the early rounds are the juice. The first round proper to be played out over the long weekend is looking, well, proper. And on Saturday at 3pm GMT, a proper time, 31 ties will kick off. No VAR, either. At the stage when the bottom two Football League divisions join the competition, focus remains on those non-league clubs fighting for the honour of the pyramid … John Aloisi winning or choking​ the Chinese Super League , a league so ‘super’ that nine of all 16 clubs in it started the season on negative points due to ‘match-fixing, gambling and corruption’ by the way, and the league leaders not even scoring a single goal in seven hours, is really not something to lay upon someone with a bad hangover. Apropos of nothing, if anyone has any objections to my views on the Chinese Super League, please address any correspondence to: Mr K Mbappé, Madrid (there’s no point two of us getting into trouble)” – Noble Francis. As a man of a certain age frequently being reminded of how out of date I am, the recent readers’ letters regarding technical solutions to shirt-pulling (Football Daily letters passim) concerns triggered distant memories. In late 1991 I was working in the Patents Advice Centre, Newcastle Central Library. A gentleman asked for help to possibly patent an ‘invention’: a football shirt with the seams held together by Velcro, so that any tug would ‘open’ the seam and provide clear evidence to the referee of illegal cloth gathering. As I helped him search for possible equivalent innovations in our paper database (yes kids!) we chatted amiably until I asked how he had come to this seemingly simple yet brilliant innovation. He paused, reddened and began to exhale with elevated pressure: ‘Did you see Arsenal the other night? Tony Adams? Disgraceful. It should never be allowed! item.title: ‘In moments of pain, football comes together’: Spain says goodbye to Jesús de Miguel
item.description: Only 3,587 people live in his family’s village but the streets of Navahermosa were fuller yet quieter to mourn the Tenerife striker at his funeral The narrow streets of Navahermosa in La Mancha were fuller than they have ever been on Thursday afternoon and quieter too. Silence accompanied the funeral cortege as its made way from the funeral home to the parish church of San Miguel Arcángel carrying Jesús de Miguel Alameda, “Demi”, the Tenerife striker who died after an on-field collision with the Andorra goalkeeper Jesús Owono three days earlier. Only 3,587 people live in his family’s village but now they were joined by the game he loved. “We wanted to be close to his parents, his wife and daughter. In moments of pain, football comes together more than ever,” said Luis de la Fuente. The Spain manager did not say much else; there was not much else he could say, not much anyone could. These have been dark, desperate days, days when it was impossible to assimilate what has happened, and there will be more. “We will get through this together but we will need help, professional help,” the Tenerife president, Felipe Miñambres, said. item.title: Cristiano Ronaldo merely the latest example of a great player who couldn’t let go | Jonathan Wilson
item.description: There is no doubt his international career was an incredible one, but it would have been greater still if he had not lingered on the stage so long Nothing, perhaps, is quite so difficult for an elite sportsperson as timing their exit. It’s not easy for any person in any job to weigh the hope of having more to give with the desire not to linger beyond their usefulness, but it’s perhaps particularly hard for top athletes because unrealistic self-confidence is so essential to their success. It takes an almost unhealthy level of self-belief for anybody to make the sacrifices to get to the top, to dedicate themselves to such a precarious vocation, to overcome all the setbacks and injuries and failures. How can someone – whose whole life has been spent assuring themselves there are no odds they cannot overcome – accept that is it, that the time has come to say goodbye? The news that Cristiano Ronaldo has retired from international football brings with it, inevitably, a sadness. Sadness we will no longer see him skipping past a defender, or burying a neck-thrusting header, and sadness in that the end of the career of any great is a reminder of mortality; all things in time must pass. But there is also a sadness he timed his departure so badly. For at least three tournaments, there has been a sense of Ronaldo holding Portugal back. Continue reading...

item.title: Uefa faces political flashpoint over Sevastopol’s ascent in Russian football
item.description: Promotion to third tier for Crimean club would be clear violation of governing body’s rules amid conflict in Ukraine Uefa and Fifa face a decisive test of their appetite to punish Russia’s integration of teams from illegally occupied Ukrainian territory after FC Sevastopol, from Crimea, won promotion to the country’s professional third tier. Sevastopol were declared champions of group one in Football National League (FNL) 2B, in effect Russia’s fourth division, last month and are believed to have applied for a licence to compete at the level above. Should it be granted and they proceed to FNL 2A, it would appear a violation of Uefa rules that prohibit Crimean clubs from playing in competitions organised by the Russian Football Union (RFU). The governing body would come under severe pressure to extend sanctions on European football’s pariah state, whose club and national teams are banned from competing in international tournaments. In the immediate aftermath, the outlook for Balogun seemed rosy; an ascendant player who could muster a goal in tense games. item.title: Mourinho’s plan comes together as Real Madrid relaunch with clásico statement | Sid Lowe
item.description: It was just like old times as José Mourinho ended a night at Camp Nou with a knee slide and three points José Mourinho had already done the por qu é? , the printout and the press conference no-show in under 100 days. Now he’s done a knee slide too, and in the perfect place: back where it all began and where it can all begin again. When Kylian Mbappé scored the first in the clásico on Sunday night, Real Madrid’s manager hardly moved, sitting in the shadow of the bench – but when the striker got the second to win it with time running out, that was different. Mourinho leapt into the light, throwing himself to the grass, the knees of a 63-year-old’s trousers muddy as a schoolboy’s, stuck his tongue out and pumped his fists. He does so love it when a plan comes together. To the right of him, the bench was emptying, subs joining the players in sprinting towards the south-west corner. As they leapt about, dodging the bottles thrown towards them from the end, way, way up in the furthest corner and stuck inside a glass box like a bunch of David Blaines, the small group of Madrid fans who had come were going mad. In the main stand, a thousand phones were raised. And 600 kilometres west, back in Boadilla, Thibaut Courtois was watching his teammates from the sofa at home, presumably wrapped in a blanket and cradling a cup of Lemsip. On the morning of the biggest game there is, he awoke with flu, forced to miss out. Continue reading...

item.title: The horse that ushered in Manchester United’s tragic arc | Jonathan Wilson
item.description: There’s plenty of blame to go around at Old Trafford. Like all downfalls it started with a seemingly small, unconnected moment Sign up for our free newsletter here And so here we are again, at that point as the nights draw in and Manchester United prepare to sack a manager . Autumn: season of mists, mellow fruitfulness and a crisis at Old Trafford. Sunday’s 3-0 home defeat to Bournemouth , coming on the back of last week’s 4-1 reverse against Como, made clear what many had feared from the moment Michael Carrick was given the job on a permanent basis: that he isn’t up to it. But then, who could be? When you’ve burned through a long list of managers in 13 years, it’s perhaps worth considering whether the manager is really the problem. Could some blame perhaps go to the director of football, Jason Wilcox, or the chief executive, Omar Berrada, the people making the appointments? Or perhaps to Sir Jim Ratcliffe, the cost-cutting tax exile and minority shareholder with responsibility for sporting operations? Or to the Glazer family, who plunged the club into debt with a leveraged buyout in 2005 and have since made calamitous decision after calamitous decision, reducing the most successful club in English league history to a mid-table laughing stock with a roof that leaks symbolically ? This is an extract from Soccer Desk, a newsletter from the Guardian US. Subscribe for free here . Continue reading...

item.title: Ousmane Dembélé quietly becomes the main man after long journey to the top
item.description: The Frenchman, who has been named the best male footballer in the world by the Guardian, has benefitted from PSG’s focus on the team rather than individuals What makes a good player great, and a great player the best? This question has been occupying me since 2014, when the Guardian first asked me to contribute to its inaugural Next Generation feature . My job was to look for a France-based talent born in 1997 who could go on to have a stellar career. After a great deal of research, I narrowed it down from my shortlist of five by asking questions not about the players’ football ability, but about other attributes: resilience, adaptability, decision-making, creativity, work ethic, response to feedback and willingness to learn. Qualities we cannot see, and are harder to measure. Continue reading...
